entry.title: Editing an ext4 Partition Directly from macOS (No Linux VM Required)
entry.summary: I lost the private key for a Raspberry Pi and needed to add a new public key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys. The Pi's SD card was plugged into a Mac via a USB reader, so diskutil list could see the partitions fine — but the root filesystem was ext4, which macOS cannot mount. No spare Linux box, no VM set up, just Docker Desktop (which, on Apple Silicon, only gives you a Linux kernel inside its VM — it doesn't let a container touch a host block device like /dev/disk5s3). This is the path that worked without either of those. e2fsck, debugfs, and friends from e2fsprogs don't rely on the kernel's ext4 driver at all — they implement the ext2/3/4 on-disk format entirely in userspace and just do read()/write()/lseek() on whatever path you give them. That means they work identically whether the tar…

entry.title: How I built a multi-provider proxy for Grok Build!
entry.summary: I wanted to use Ollama and other providers with Grok Build without How it works Grok Build → GrokRoute (:8083) → Agnes / Groq / Zhipu / Laguna / Ollama The proxy is a single Python file implementing the OpenAI Proxy reads the provider config Tries providers in priority order If one fails (rate limit, timeout) — next provider takes over in 5s Streams the response back to Grok Build Non-streaming mode goes even faster: fires requests to ALL providers Quick start npm install -g grokroute Then press SPACE — Grok Build launches with multi-provider support. Key features 5+ providers: Ollama, Groq, Agnes, Zhipu, Laguna Auto-fallback: sequential with 5s timeout per provider Race mode: parallel requests, fastest response wins Web admin UI: dark theme, :8083/admin Local-only: runs on 127.0.0.1, no telemetry MIT license I was benchmarking different models for coding tasks and got tired of Source: github.com/wxstdo-boop/grokroute Happy to answer questions!

entry.title: LLMs Are Stateless. Here Is What That Actually Means for Agent Memory.
entry.summary:
LLMs Are Stateless. Here Is What That Actually Means for Agent Memory.
There is a sentence that most AI agent tutorials skip over, and it explains Between API calls, the model knows nothing. Every "memory feature" you have ever seen — ChatGPT's memory, Claude's Projects, If the LLM is stateless, then the intelligence of a long-running agent lives entirely This is not a limitation. It is a design principle. The research community has started treating it explicitly this way: MemGPT (2023) introduced the "LLM as OS" analogy: the model is a CPU,
StateFlow (2024) goes further: the agent is a Finite State Machine.
ClawVM (2026) formalises this as a virtual memory layer: the harness enforces
The consequence for memory design
If the LLM is purely a processing unit, then the quality of your agent's memory harness — the system that decides what facts to A harness that stores flat embeddings and retrieves by similarity gives you a A temporal assertion is a fact with a lifespan: subject: user_project predicate: uses_language object: Python valid_from: 2025-01-10 valid_to: 2025-06-15 ← closed when user switched to TypeScript
The harness stores this, not the LLM. The LLM never sees the old fact again valid_to is set. Active state is WHERE valid_to IS NULL. This is the model behind Smriti — an open-source The LLM is not the agent. The harness is the agent. Build the harness well. MIT license. PostgreSQL-backed. Open source.

entry.title: NextAuth v5 sessions: JWT or database? Untangling the adapter-driven switch with a production config
entry.summary:
This is a translation of my original article in Japanese: Qiita I run NextAuth (Auth.js) v5 in two indie products (web + iOS). They work, but for a long time I could not have answered a simple question: is my session a JWT or a database row? After digging in, it turns out there are really only two rules to remember: The session strategy switches implicitly based on whether you configured an adapter (none = jwt, present = database) The Credentials provider does not create database sessions, so it requires an explicit strategy: "jwt"
